events.label: Reddit (RDDT) joins S&P 500 — passive demand concentrated at Aug 17 closing auction
events.note: Announced Aug 13 after close; RDDT +12% pre-market Aug 14 (~$177), replacing AvalonBay Communities. Passive funds tracking the S&P 500 must hold RDDT before the Aug 18 open; the Aug 17 closing auction concentrates the mechanical buying. Post-mechanics test: RDDT holding above $177 for two sessions after Aug 18 = fundamental demand (advertising durability in AI-search environment) supports the passive bid. Reversion below $158 (pre-announcement close) within two sessions = purely mechanical pop. SPCX Nasdaq-100 inclusion precedent (July): mechanical gains can unwind substantially without fundamental support.

events.label: SPCX next staggered tranche (~7%) — second unlock after Aug 6 first tranche
events.note: Updated Aug 14 morning: SPCX $142.31 (Aug 13 close); August 20 is 6 days away. Macro has improved materially: September hike odds ~33%, CPI core 2.5%, PPI 0.0%. Oil triggers remain active: WTI $81.27 (above $79), Brent $87.18 (above $85). Rate relief has been absorbed above $128. Front-run signal: close below $120 on elevated volume before Aug 20. Morgan Stanley $140, Bernstein $248, Citi $200 targets. October Q3 earnings (Starlink profitability) is the narrative anchor. The Aug 14 30Y drift to ~5.19% is a modestly constructive development for the rate-compression side of the absorption thesis, but oil trigger clearance remains the blocking condition.

events.label: NVDA Q2 FY27 earnings (est.) — CSCO and AMAT altitude-plus-China templates raise the bar
events.note: Updated Aug 14 morning: NVDA pre-market ~$225.09, holding $225 support for second session. CSCO extended to −8.5% cumulative and AMAT fell −3.89% AH (EPS beat, revenue slight miss, Q4 guide $10.25B). Aug 14 analysis adds China equipment demand softening to the AMAT signal — altitude ceiling now has two independent components. NVDA's China exposure is separately managed via export-controlled Hopper H20, so the China component does not directly apply. The bar for Aug 26: gross margin above 78% and guide visibly ahead of the most optimistic sell-side scenario — meeting the minimum (GM above 76%, in-line guide) is established as insufficient. September hike odds ~33%, 30Y ~5.19% pre-market (drifting lower). Jackson Hole (Aug 27) begins the day after the print — no de-risk window.

events.label: Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium (Aug 27–29) — Warsh keynote; September odds at 33%
events.note: Updated Aug 14 morning: September hike odds ~33% (lowest since pre-ECI spike) after CPI core 2.5%, PPI 0.0%, and NFP −23K. 30Y at ~5.19% pre-market (first compression below 5.24% in 16 sessions) but still 4bps above the 5.15% de-escalation target. Warsh has described his keynote as a 'blank piece of paper' — no pre-commitment. Market is asymmetrically positioned: from 33%, a speech validating 30Y persistence at current levels has more room to move September odds upward than a soft speech has to move them lower. NVDA earnings land Aug 26 — one day before the keynote, no de-risk window. Key signal: 30Y close relative to 5.20% on Aug 14 is the first read on whether the bond market is moving or holding ahead of Warsh's remarks.

events.label: SPCX 180-day IPO lock-up expiry (approx.) — terminal insider/early-investor float unlock
events.note: ~180 days after the June 12 debut. Lock-up expiries are the known supply overhang for hot IPOs. Context after Aug 6-7: 20% first tranche absorbed at $105-$115; next tranches scheduled Aug 20 and late September. Q3 Starlink profitability (~October call) is the only fundamental catalyst that could revalue the lockup discount before the December terminal release. SPCX Q2: $18.37B capex vs $7.81B revenue; AI segment $2.56B (+247% YoY).

events.label: OpenAI IPO — target window H1 2027 after 2026 delay
events.note: OpenAI delayed its anticipated 2026 IPO to H1 2027 (announced June 26, 2026). PLTR's 149% US commercial growth, AMD's $6.7B data-center (+107%), and SpaceX's exclusive Nvidia commitment ($15.83B AI capex) confirm the enterprise AI adoption underlying OpenAI's revenue model. NVDA circular financing disclosure ($250B OpenAI backstop) remains the unresolved structural question that may surface in S-1 filings.
